purpose: Test whether preseason-known role and opportunity-allocation features close the remaining FSFFL Native gap to established external projection systems without training on external forecasts or target-season realized usage.

diagnostic_basis.native_vs_external: The verified Native-vs-FFToday benchmark shows the largest stable remaining gap in QB, then RB and WR, while post-hoc injury diagnostics indicate injury seasons do not explain the gap away.
diagnostic_basis.external_methodology_clue: Established projection systems commonly begin from expected role/snap/opportunity allocation. This is treated only as a feature hypothesis; no external projection values become Native training labels.

prior_team_opportunity_share.description: Player share of the immediately prior completed season's team opportunity at the relevant position/stat family.

opening_team_vacated_opportunity.description: Share of the target-season opening team's prior-year opportunity attributable to players not present on that target-season opening depth chart. Uses only prior-season stats plus target-season opening depth-chart membership.

role_share_interactions.description: Interactions between opening first-team/depth role and prior opportunity share, allowing the model to distinguish returning starters from high-history players who lost role.

allowed: prior completed-season player and team statistics
target-season opening/pre-Week-1 depth rank or first-team role
roster departures identifiable from the opening depth-chart snapshot
forbidden: target-season realized routes, carries, targets or pass attempts

validation_policy.base_model: current Native V2 production-candidate feature bundle by position
validation_policy.retain_feature_family_only_if: material mean improvement with multi-season stability; intuitive football relevance is not sufficient
validation_policy.external_benchmark_followup: Any retained family must subsequently be re-run on the exact Native-vs-external common cohort to confirm it closes external residual error rather than merely beating persistence.
